body: Given the specific scope, might this be better as a utility function in `@gdscript`?
I would more like operator `//` like in Python..

In my opinion, we should first decide on the long-term future of how we want division to work in Godot 5.0.

If we want to change it to a more typical floating-point division for scripting languages, then both `intdiv()` and the `//` operator make sense in 5.0 (however, the `//` operator would be confusing in 4.x, due to `int / int == int`).

If we want to keep the current behavior, the very existence of the `INTEGER_DIVISION` warning seems contradictory. In that case, we should deprecate it in 4.x and remove it in 5.0. Also, `intdiv()` and the `//` operator would be confusing, given that `int / int` is already integer division.

> Given the specific scope, might this be better as a utility function in `@gdscript`?

Note that the division is performed in `Variant`, not GDScript (for example, this also applies to the `Expression` class). So, it seems reasonable to me to place this function in `@GlobalScope`, not `@GDScript`.

Personally, I would prefer the first option. I'm not familiar with a wide variety of scripting languages, but I can see that at least Python 3.13.5 performs floating-point division even when both operands are ints:
```py
Python 3.13.5 (main, Jun 11 2025, 15:36:57) [Clang 17.0.0 (clang-1700.0.13.3)] on darwin
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> 1 / 2
0.5
```
Furthermore, GDScript is often marketed as a beginner-friendly, intuitive scripting language. Many new users are likely to recall that from their math education, 1/2 is 0.5, so they will type `1 / 2` into their script assuming it will evaluate to `0.5`. They'll find it confusing that this instead evaluates to `1`, and that in order to get what they wanted, they had to instead write at least one of the operands as floats. The `//` operator stands out from the traditional `/` operator, so if they see it in a piece of code, they will (hopefully) recognize that it must mean something different.

> I would more like operator `//` like in Python..

In the long run, I agree as I explained above. My hope with this PR was more to provide a stop-gap solution for now, that allows integer division to be performed in the cases where it's intended, without needing to annotate the line with a `@warning_ignore` or change project settings to ignore integer division as a whole (in case it accidentally happens where you *don't* want it).


> > Given the specific scope, might this be better as a utility function in `@gdscript`?
> 
> Note that the division is performed in `Variant`, not GDScript (for example, this also applies to the `Expression` class). So, it seems reasonable to me to place this function in `@GlobalScope`, not `@GDScript`.

Happy accident, I suppose! I've not worked with the `Expression` class before, and just had GDScript in mind when I was putting this together. I'd been considering following AST's thoughts and moving it to `@GDScript` for this reason, but if it has more benefits in `@GlobalScope` then it can certainly stay. My motivation for placing it in `@GlobalScope` initially was just that there are many other math-related functions there already (`abs`, `ceil`, `clamp`, `exp`, `log`, etc) so I thought it'd fit best alongside those ones.

It's important that there _be_ a stopgap, but imo a clarifying pattern like in #107642 makes a bit more sense for a stopgap than adding a dedicated function, as this feels more permanent, if that makes sense
Yeah when I first saw this PR I wanted to comment that we don't need a dedicated function since you can just do `int(a / b)` but I tested and indeed that doesn't remove the warning.

I left more of my thoughts on the `int(a / b)` approach in that PR's thread, but overall I agree that I think `a / b` emitting the `INTEGER_DIVISION` warning and telling the user to do `a // b` instead would be the best option (with `a / b` eventually being changed in 5.0 to never perform integer division). 

As for how that relates to this PR: if the `a // b` solution could be implemented relatively soon, then I think it'd make sense to just go ahead with that and close this `intdiv()` PR. However, if changes such as the addition of a new `//` operator are out of scope for the foreseeable future, then *some* stopgap solution (be it `intdiv(a, b)`, `int(a / b)`, or something else) would be very nice to have in the meantime.

> this feels more permanent

In my opinion, we need greater permanence and certainty in this matter. We should decide what behavior we ultimately want and base our strategy on that.

Because our design currently straddles two opposing lines: we want `int / int == int` (we consider this correct, normal, and right) and at the same time generate a warning, discouraging use it at all. See also my [comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/107642#issuecomment-3837502833).

> `int(a / b)`

I'm not sure this is a good idea:

First, it's implicit. `intdiv(a, b)` clearly[^1] states what this code does. `int(a / b)` leaves room for assumptions. You only know that the result will be an `int`, but you don't know how the division operator works. A programmer unfamiliar with Godot might assume that `a / b` returns a `float`, and `int()` truncates it (like in Python and most other scripting languages). But that's not true! `a / b` already performs integer division and returns an `int`. `int()` doesn't do anything useful; it's just a crude patch on a flaw in the current design.

Second, if I'm not mistaken, `int()` call generates runtime code (unless the argument is a constant expression). Yes, we could optimize this case, but I still think it's a bad idea to write code that isn't actually executed for its intended purpose, but simply serves to cover up language design flaws, false positives warnings, compiler bugs, and so on.

[^1]: Not quite. Because there are two types of integer division and two types of remainder, depending on whether the remainder's sign is determined by the dividend or the divisor. For example, in Haskell, these operations are called `quot`/`div` (quotient/division) and `rem`/`mod` (remainder/modulo).

Given that this could easily be used everywhere, why not simplify the function name to e.g.:
1. `div(a, b)` (since we don't expect a float version of div anyway, if I understand correctly); or
2. `divi(a, b)` (following the pattern of floori, ceili, randi, signi, clampi; with i suffix; also one can ignore the i and think of divi as an abbreviation of division, so it shouldn't bother much); or
3. `idiv(a, b)` (following the pattern of fmod) -- this might make more sense since like fmod, it's not an overload of a similar variant function, instead it's an operation meant for ints by its nature

I normally prefer Java-like verbosity in method names (and I'd agree intdiv gives more clarity), but in this case it's more like a math operator (which is expected to be concise) and it seems like there's already a pattern which could make it more consistent?

Though if the intention is to deprecate it for `//` eventually in 5.0, I guess it doesn't matter much.

Also, if we're comparing it to Haskell, IIUC `int / int` in Godot matches the "quot" behavior instead of the "div" behavior? So maybe calling it "quot" and maybe making 2 functions so as to also have div (like `posmod` and `%`) could make sense too? Or call it `div` but use the "div" implementation, and later when `//` is introduced, that one could be the "quot" implementation -- i.e. make it so this "div" function is meant to stay and not be deprecated later.
